Local CSS syntax fixes and performance
Recorded 2026-11-01

All 173 local-fix candidate assertions now pass the selected syntax audit:
  7 intrinsic flex-basis values through the existing native Size parser
  3 z-index numeric-math values through the native number parser
114 retained selector AST constraints
 49 generated-content/counter constraints using shared existing AST consumers

Fresh baseline: 16,230 / 18,466 assertions pass (87.89%); 2,236 mismatches.
After fixes:    16,406 / 18,469 assertions pass (88.83%); 2,063 mismatches.
There are zero new mismatch keys. Three previously unrepresented assertions
are now classified as passing by the earlier invalid-value checks. On the
unchanged baseline selection, 16,403 / 18,466 pass (88.83%). The earlier saved
audit had ten fewer classified passing assertions; those ten are not credited
to this change.

These are assertion counts from extracted literal CSS helpers. Computed-style
helper calls still check syntax only. They are not complete WPT file passes,
computed-value checks, rendering coverage, or a new overall image-suite result.

Implementation

Lightning CSS remains unchanged and the sole CSS parser. The new value routes
serialize native tokens and call existing native value parsers. Intrinsic sizes
use the existing preferred-size conversion. Numeric math rounds integer ties
toward positive infinity and saturates at engine integer bounds; literal
fractions remain invalid and non-finite results stay outside the new path.

Selector validation inspects the native AST for retained :has() constraints,
required function arguments, nonfunctional pseudo-elements used as functions,
and picker identifiers. Uppercase SELECT remains valid. Forgiving :is/:where
lists retain their existing handling; this is not a replacement selector parser.

Existing counter argument/list consumers are shared between syntax and renderer
conversion. Custom counter styles remain separate from rendering support.
Unsupported images, reversed counters and unresolved expressions retain their
existing handling. The attr() change rejects empty arguments; it does not claim
full modern attr() grammar support.

Supported content/counter eligibility and native value fallback eligibility are
cached during stylesheet preparation. Conversions live in their property-family
handlers. Ordinary declarations avoid the initial unrelated-property lookup.

Validation

- Existing style tests: 305 passed, including allocation checks.
- Existing declaration-validation tests: 32 passed.
- cargo check -p skrift-style --offline passed.
- The full pinned syntax audit scanned 35,417 files / 32,021 literal calls,
  with zero dependency parser panics and zero new mismatch keys.
- The diagnostic audit exits 101 because 2,063 existing mismatches remain;
  this is not reported as an all-green WPT suite.
- New modules pass rustfmt checks. No test code or expectations were changed.
- No image comparisons were rerun. Rendering records remain unchanged.

Performance

Positive changes below mean slower. Changes are median percentages from 15
paired process runs per workload, alternating before/after order, pinned to
CPU 6. Existing benchmark sources were compiled unchanged with rustc opt-level=2,
identical native dependencies and identical freshly rebuilt support crates.
Final measurements comprise 300 process runs; 540 intermediate runs are also
retained. Each invocation has its own warmups and measured iterations.

EPUB/workload totals sum the five fixture medians per process, rather than
representing one page. Cold means an uncached author style program with warmed
default CSS and machine caches. CPU frequency/boost was uncontrolled on a shared
machine. Intervals below are diagnostic 95% bootstrap ranges of paired median
changes, without multiple-comparison correction; they do not prove performance
equality when they contain zero.

Workload                      Change       Bootstrap range       Assessment
Plain cascade                   -1.37%   [  -4.11%,   +1.28%]   inconclusive
Variables/inline cascade        +0.33%   [  -1.09%,   +0.82%]   inconclusive
EPUB, uncached author program   +0.44%   [  -2.09%,   +1.67%]   inconclusive
EPUB, cached author program     -1.34%   [  -4.18%,   +2.45%]   inconclusive
Content/counter, uncached       -9.05%   [  -9.58%,   -5.15%]   speedup
Content/counter, cached        -14.27%   [ -14.92%,  -12.55%]   speedup
New values, uncached (*)        +4.55%   [  -6.84%,   +8.32%]   inconclusive
New values, cached (*)          -0.66%   [  -5.57%,   +1.67%]   inconclusive
Normalization                   -8.23%   [ -29.01%,   +1.35%]   inconclusive
Normalization with retry        +1.38%   [  +0.37%,   +4.14%]   slowdown

Individual EPUB samples with wholly positive timing ranges:
  epub-cold / reference/style_total_us: +1.21% [+0.06%, +2.82%]

The small normalization-retry and reference-EPUB slowdowns remain recorded.
The equivalent content/counter/:has workload is about 9-14% faster following
eligibility caching. Ordinary aggregate EPUB/cascade timing ranges include zero.

(*) The new-value workload adds flex-basis:min-content and z-index:calc(3 - 2).
The baseline ignores those declarations; the changed build applies them.
This includes additional feature work and is not an equivalent-output regression
measurement. Its positive uncached point estimate remains recorded as
inconclusive. Allocation counts and per-sample stage timings, including all
positive results, are retained in local-fix-performance.json.

The new native-value paths also allocate while serializing/reparsing native
tokens. In the first generated fixture, allocation counts rise from 6,863 to
7,908 (+15.2%) without author-program reuse and from 1,863 to 2,524 (+35.5%)
with reuse. Peak tracked bytes increase about 0.2-0.8%. The baseline skips the
new values, so these are added-feature costs. Equivalent content/counter and
ordinary small-classic allocation/peak counts stay unchanged. Complete counts
for every fixture are retained in the performance JSON.

Intermediate regressions found and corrected

The initial full audit caught rejecting ::picker(SELECT); case handling was
corrected. An existing test caught five unnecessary allocations when rejecting
a string counter-style argument; a primitive-token guard restored rejection
without allocations. First timing runs showed roughly 3% synthetic cascade
slowdown; later runs exposed repeated per-element counter validation. The
unrelated lookup, central dispatch branch and repeated validation were removed
or cached. Intermediate measurement summaries and raw runs remain in the record.

Remaining work and evidence

The remaining 2,063 mismatches comprise 178 confirmed native-parser blocks and
1,885 unresolved assertions. Original observations remain in css-syntax.jsonl;
173 entries now have fixed_in_syntax_audit status and a resolution, while their
original keys/actual/native fields remain historical. Exact fixed keys and
before/after syntax outcomes are in local-fix-results.jsonl. The original
investigation report and native equality/source evidence are retained.

local-fix-report.json records counts, source hashes and scope.
local-fix-performance.json records methods, all timing/allocation comparisons,
intermediate stages and both generated CSS workloads. Compressed raw runs are
in local-fix-performance-runs.jsonl.gz. Original build commands, complete logs
and the before-source snapshot are retained on disk at:
/home/johan/.cache/html-wpt-local-fixes

No Lightning CSS changes, second CSS text parser, test code, expectation edits,
capability exclusion edits, rendering comparison changes or GPUI changes were
introduced. All new build outputs and compiler scratch use the disk-backed
cache directory above.
